name: Madkhalism
summary: Madkhalism is a strand of Salafism named for the Saudi scholar Rabi' al-Madkhali. It teaches unconditional public loyalty to the Muslim ruler, rejects protest, revolution, party politics and democracy, and fights rival Islamist currents, the Muslim Brotherhood and Qutbists above all, by scholarly refutation. Its aim is a purified creed and community before any state, and its teachers support state counter-terrorism work.
scope: The transnational quietist-loyalist current around Rabi' al-Madkhali as documented in scholarship on Indonesia, Philadelphia, Libya and Madkhali's refutation of Sayyid Qutb (2020-2024), with Indonesian Madkhali teachers' own sermons and writings as reported by Sunarwoto. It excludes other Salafi currents (jihadist, Sahwa and non-Madkhali purists), and Libyan armed Madkhali factions, whose fatwas conflict. Primary texts are known only through scholars' quotations; no full Madkhali book was available.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Madkhalis hold that the Islamic state is built on the Quran and the Sunna as the early generations understood them and praise Saudi Arabia for applying them; Sunarwoto sets this out in the account of Ba'abduh's conditions for a caliphate.

separate-church-state.rationale: Madkhalis define an Islamic state by implemented Islamic law and public Islamic symbols and hold Saudi Arabia up as the model, which excludes a strict separation of religion and state.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Sunarwoto reports that Madkhalis separate parliamentary democracy, where the majority is the source of authority, from shura, where authority rests on sharia, and call democracy disobedience to God.

consent-of-governed.rationale: For Madkhalis the only requirement for a ruler's legitimacy is that he be a Muslim, whether or not his rule follows sharia; popular consent plays no part and democratic choice is called un-Islamic.

democracy-best.rationale: Luqman Ba'abduh has consistently declared democracy a form of disobedience to God, and Madkhalis hold parliamentary democracy to be an un-Islamic system.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Madkhalis hold that a Muslim ruler's failure to rule by divine law is only minor unbelief (kufr dun kufr) and does not remove the duty to obey; rebellion needs clear proof of apostasy plus the strength to succeed, and senior teachers say these conditions are not met.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The doctrine requires obedience even to a flawed or sinful Muslim ruler, and scholars report unquestioning loyalty even to governments using extreme violence; only clear apostasy lifts it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Madkhalis reject revolution and coups as a route to an Islamic state and told followers to stay out of the 2011 uprisings, though doctrine allows rebellion against a clearly apostate ruler if strong enough, which they say is never the case now.

direct-action.rationale: Madkhalis hold that protest marches and similar opposition to the government contradict Islamic ethics, and they decline party politics and revolution as well.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Madkhalis abstain from elections, parties and protest and say they confine themselves to outreach, purification and education, though Sunarwoto shows they are active in polemics against rival currents.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Ba'abduh says a kingdom, republic or parliamentary system can all count as an Islamic state, and Indonesian Madkhalis defend the Saudi monarchy as an Islamic state and guardian of tawhid.

clerical-rule.rationale: Madkhalis hold that any Muslim ruler is the walī l-amr whatever his religious learning, and one teacher sets a clear hierarchy of state over scholars, though scholars share authority in religious matters.

elective-rulers.rationale: Madkhalis accept any form of Muslim rule, including the Saudi monarchy, and reject popular choice as a source of authority, so election of rulers is not required.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Madkhalis obey a ruler because he is a Muslim holding office, a sinful and flawed one included, and not as a sacred person of divine descent.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Madkhalis teach loyalty to the Muslim ruler as an individual legal obligation (farḍ ʿayn), though the duty rests on revelation and lapses where the ruler commands disobedience to God.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Madkhali ruled the Maluku jihad individually obligatory for Muslims under attack, and Indonesian teachers say Muslims must defend the Land of Islam, though they add that jihad needs the ruler's proclamation.

religious-offensive-war.rationale: As reported by Arikewuyo, Madkhali argues from Q 2:193 that Muslim authorities are commanded to fight non-Muslims until they embrace Islam, echoing classical scholars.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Madkhali rejects Qutb's claim of equal rights for non-Muslims, citing Quranic verses against equalising believers with disbelievers, the rule that a Muslim is not killed for killing a non-Muslim, and the Covenant of Umar.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Madkhali treats the Covenant of Umar, which bars non-Muslims from publicly displaying their faith's symbols, as binding authority and argues that Qutb's religious freedom would perpetuate infidelity.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Madkhali argues Muslim authorities are to fight non-Muslims until they embrace Islam and that Qutb's freedom of religion perpetuates unbelief, which excludes equal standing for other religions.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Madkhalis hold to the understanding of the Quran and Sunna fixed by the early generations, and Madkhali treats the Covenant of Umar as a fixed authority where Qaradawi calls it changeable state policy.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Goshey reports that Salafi affiliates rely on the Quran, the Sunna and the Pious Predecessors' understanding and reject speculative theology (ʿilm al-kalām); Madkhalis likewise condemn philosophy in the national curriculum.

religion-illusion.rationale: Madkhalis treat their creed as the revealed truth and the basis of a complete way of life, so a view of religion as a consoling illusion is the opposite of their position.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: A state promoting atheism is the opposite of the Islamic state Madkhalis hold up, defined by Muslim majority, public Islamic symbols and implemented Islamic law.

patriotic-education.rationale: Madkhalis refuse the civic education subject because it teaches nationalism, which they say contradicts universal Muslim solidarity, and run schools outside the national curriculum.

nation-first.rationale: Madkhali teachers say Muslims must defend Islam and the Land of Islam rather than the national homeland, and that nationalism cannot cure radicalism; their loyalty is to the Muslim community.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Madkhalis hold that parliamentary democracy does not fit Islam and set shura on sharia against it, so a civilization may have its own form of government.

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: Madkhalis condemn the Bali bombers, al-Qaeda and the Islamic State as terrorists and khawarij and support state counter-terrorism work.

gradual-change.rationale: Following al-Albani, Madkhalis hold that the Islamic state starts in each Muslim's heart and not through revolution, party politics or coups, and they obey established authorities.

restore-past-order.rationale: The programme is a return to the Quran and Sunna as the early generations understood them, and the caliphate 'on the prophetic principle'.

more-religion-public.rationale: Madkhalis name public Islamic symbols and implemented Islamic law as marks of an Islamic state and praise Saudi Arabia for upholding them.
